content: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is categorized into stages based on estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) values. Stage G1 corresponds to an eGFR of 90 mL/min/1.73m² or higher. Stage G2 is defined by an eGFR between 60 and 89 mL/min/1.73m². Stage G3a includes eGFR values ranging from 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73m², while Stage G3b encompasses eGFR values between 30 and 44 mL/min/1.73m². Stage G4 is characterized by an eGFR of 15 to 29 mL/min/1.73m², and Stage G5 is defined as an eGFR below 15 mL/min/1.73m². The level of albuminuria, which refers to the presence of albumin in the urine, is an additional parameter used to stratify the risk associated with CKD. Albuminuria levels are critical in assessing both the risk of cardiovascular complications and the likelihood of CKD progression. Clinical guidelines emphasize the importance of using both eGFR and albuminuria levels in combination to accurately diagnose and manage CKD. This dual approach provides a more comprehensive understanding of the disease and informs treatment strategies.
